summary: Three high-risk security findings require code fixes before testing: login CSRF, unbounded poll limiter memory, and an unprotected mutating poll endpoint.
validation: PR #95 CI is green: Go, container, vulnerability, secret, and artifact checks passed.
Review covered commit aac06dc against main; no live systems, secrets, or deployments were accessed.
blockers: Unauthenticated password login lacks bootstrap CSRF and Origin validation.
Unique invalid poll cookies allocate unbounded rate-limiter entries.
GET polling performs authentication state transitions without CSRF or Origin protection.
next_action: Route to code: fix REV-001 through REV-003, add regression tests, then rerun review.

issues.title: Password fallback permits login CSRF
issues.details: internal/publicapi/server.go:login issues a session without bootstrap CSRF or Origin validation. A cross-site request can force the victim into an attacker-selected Jellyfin account, causing wrong-user Google linking. Require bootstrap CSRF and same-origin validation; test all aliases.

issues.title: Poll limiter has unbounded key growth
issues.details: quickConnectStatus keys the limiter by an unvalidated cookie hash before flow lookup. RateLimiter.entries has no global eviction, so unique invalid cookies grow memory without bound despite the 256-flow cap. Validate first and add bounded expiry/eviction.

issues.title: Mutating GET poll lacks CSRF protection
issues.details: quickConnectStatus performs Connect, AuthenticateWithQuickConnect, and session issuance on GET without CSRF or Origin checks. SameSite=Lax permits cross-site top-level navigation with the flow cookie. Use CSRF-protected POST polling or equivalent strict origin controls.
